description: The recorded KiCad Routing Tools plan for the microphone array. Every
ordinary signal on this board is routed by this stage and by nothing
else: no hand-drawn copper, no coordinate repairs, no post-route via
nudging. If a routed candidate fails, the fix belongs in gen_pcb.py, in
the generated keep-outs, or in this file - never in the board.
Widths, clearances, via sizes and layers are deliberately NOT restated
here. route.py reads them from the sibling .kicad_pro net classes, which
is the same source gen_pcb.py and the validator use, so there is one
place to change them and no way for the three to disagree.

policy.locked_input_copper: every track and via gen_pcb.py produced is locked before routing
scope: A net is in scope only if gen_pcb.py leaves it unfinished. That is not
a convenience: route.py's post-route cleanup prunes dead ends and
redundant copper across every net it was asked to route, and it counts
the input file's own copper as a removal candidate. Asked to route +5V,
which the generator had already finished, it deleted a 1.6 mm leg of
the bus and left the rest dangling. Nets the generator completes are
therefore excluded outright, and the pre-route DRC report is the check
that this list still matches what the generator actually finishes: a
net that stops being complete shows up as an unconnected item.

reason: route.py otherwise rewrites the sibling .kicad_pro DRC floor to
whatever clearance it actually managed to route at. An earlier run
silently dropped the Default class to 0.175 mm and a later one to
0.1 mm, which is below every net class on this board. The flag keeps
the project's real limits authoritative; a stage that cannot route
inside them must fail loudly instead.
route.py walks sets while deciding what to route first, so its order
of work varies between processes. Pinning the hash seed removes the
part of that caused by string hashing. It is not a complete fix -
sets of objects still iterate in address order - and two runs of this
plan still differ on about seven of eighty-three nets: same via
count, total copper within 0.1 percent, every gate passing either
way. The generated pre-route board IS byte-identical run to run; it
is the routing that is equivalent rather than repeated, and the gates

stages.purpose: the nets gen_pcb.py leaves open: host SPI and control, the ESD taps, the clock buffer outputs, the analogue and clock supplies

excluded_because.GND: implemented as inner-layer zones plus generated stitching vias
excluded_because.PDM_CLK_B*: length-matched branch trees, pre-routed and locked
excluded_because.PDM_CLK_IN: buffer fan-in, pre-routed and locked; F.Cu, zero vias
excluded_because.PDM_CLK_FPGA: clock root, pre-routed and locked; F.Cu, zero vias
excluded_because.AUDIO_MCLK: master clock, pre-routed and locked; F.Cu, zero vias
excluded_because.MCLK_OSC: oscillator to its series resistor, pre-routed and locked
excluded_because.PDM_D?: data spokes, finished by the generator: radial on F.Cu to a legalised handover via, then across the socket rows on B.Cu
excluded_because.MIC_VDD_*: microphone supply ring, finished by the generator
excluded_because.MIC_DOUT_*: per-channel escapes through the 0.566 mm ring corners, finished by the generator
excluded_because.+5V: input chain and both supply buses, finished by the generator
excluded_because.PI_5V: Pi header feed through the fuse, finished by the generator
excluded_because.5V_FUSED: fuse to Schottky, finished by the generator

post.reason: vias added by the router pierce the ground planes; without a refill every one of them reads as a zone clearance violation
